transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um, I keep rechecking and fixing how I look before I go out or get on camera, and it’s starting to make me late and stressed all the time. My older sister actually noticed how anxious I've been getting about it and encouraged me to come get an evaluation.

Do you feel like you are checking your appearance to prevent a specific dreaded outcome or to follow a strict internal rule, or is your primary concern that there is an actual physical defect in your appearance that others will notice?

It's definitely about actual flaws in my appearance that I'm worried others will notice, like my jaw looking crooked and my skin looking really bad. I get stuck in front of the mirror or taking test selfies just trying to adjust myself until I feel "less ugly" before anyone else sees me. It's not about preventing some other bad outcome, I'm just really self-conscious about those specific things.
Do you feel that your concern with these specific flaws is excessive or irrational, or are you firmly convinced that these physical imperfections are truly noticeable and unattractive to others?

I'm not really sure, it's hard to say. To me, the flaws feel very real and noticeable, but I do know my friends say they don't see anything wrong at all. It just feels so obvious to me when I look in the mirror, even if others tell me otherwise.

When you are not currently looking in a mirror or checking your appearance, are you able to acknowledge that your perception of these flaws might be exaggerated or distorted, even if they still feel very real to you in the moment?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. Even when I'm not looking in a mirror, the flaws still feel so real to me that it's hard to think they aren't actually there. I know my friends tell me they don't see anything wrong, but it's just really tough to shake the feeling that it looks bad.
If you saw someone else with the exact same features you are worried about on your own face, would you think they looked flawed or unattractive, or would they look normal to you?
I haven't really thought about that, to be honest. I'm not sure how I would view those features on someone else, since I'm usually just so focused on how they look on my own face.

If you were to see someone else with the exact same jawline or skin texture that you are worried about, would you personally judge them as being unattractive or flawed, or would you find them to look perfectly normal?

I think I would probably think they look perfectly normal. It's just different when I look at myself—I can't help but feel like it looks really bad on me, even if I wouldn't judge someone else for it.
